chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Black comedy acts of the 1920s: sketches and blackouts
summary: He recalls military and hospital sketches, blackouts and Pigmeat Markham at the Apollo, without remembering jokes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What kind of comedy were they doing in these acts?
Comedy like sketches they had, blackouts they had, they did military sketches. It's hard to tell you the comedy acts they had, but it was really terrific comedy.
Was Pig Meat Markham around at that time?
Yeah, Pig Meat Markham was around at that time, he was working in New York at the Apollo.
Can you tell me about some of those acts? Can you remember the kind of acts that they did, the kind of jokes they had?
I can't remember the jokes they had, but they had quite a few good comedy acts, different ones I could say, and naturally they had acts that you can't explain their material at all.
Well, what kind of subject matter, what were they dealing with, what did the humor deal with?

They were dealing like one guy is sick and he's in the hospital and got to get an operation and they're going to drill and one of the soldiers next to another soldier says, "Major, make (so-and-so) put his wing down." He would have his arm up and the guy would make him put his arm down because it didn't sound so good when he had his arm up. That was some of the things they did -- but it's hard to explain it to you.
